Summary (full text)

Camera wyze-t20x-jxf23 (T20) in the light box with the SpyderCheckr 24 chart, lamps 3000 K. Both stacks ran on the same camera, the same chart position and the same light: the open stack (open-tx-isp + OpenIMP + streamer) and the vendor stack (Ingenic ISP module + vendor libimp + streamer built for it), one after the other.

Result: 54 pass, 6 fail (1 invalid by test setup, 5 issues), 97 info/warn, 1 planned checks not run in these runs.

Failed checks: frame luma p1_night (AE target, default comp 128) (open 67.6, vendor 78.6; pass = open within +-10 % of vendor); NV12 Y temporal std at gain 1 (open 1.410, vendor 1.067; pass = open <= vendor x 1.1); NV12 Y temporal std at gain 16 (open 1.663, vendor 1.328; pass = open <= vendor x 1.1); NV12 Y temporal std at gain max (open 1.724, vendor 1.369; pass = open <= vendor x 1.1); OSD text item appears (open changed 1.9 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 % , vendor changed 1.5 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 % ; pass = > 2 % of the item box changes by > 40 and > 5 x the no-text A/A pair; box 764,482-988,566; pass = > 2 % of the item box changes by > 40 and > 5 x the no-text A/A pair; box 764,482-988,566; open repeated: 2/2 failed (values changed 1.9 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 % | changed 1.6 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 %); vendor repeated: 2/2 failed (values changed 1.5 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 % | changed 1.4 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 %)); time to a stable picture: WB preset 3 at 3000 K (s) (open >66, vendor 28; not stable within 60 s; 3 shots 3 s apart within 0.5 % R/G, B/G and 1 Y).

Passed: frame luma p1_day (AE target, default comp 128); chart grey RG (AWB, 1.0 = neutral); chart grey BG (AWB, 1.0 = neutral); p1_day dE00 mean, unclipped patches; p1_day dE00 mean, grey-normalised; grey row tone slope; MTF50 median of 8 chart edges (cycles/pixel); 10-90 % edge rise median (px); H.264 FixQP 25: decodes clean; H.264 FixQP 25: blocking / ghosting flags; ...

How to read: "pass" means the open stack is equal to or better than the vendor stack within the tolerance named in each row; matched-exposure rows (A2) compare the same integration time and gain on both stacks, read back from the ISP.

A5 Encoder (H.264): open vs vendor, same settings

Cells = open / vendor. Static chart scene, lamps on, day pinned, streamer restarted per case with a /tmp conf. Bytes per frame and P/I from ffprobe -show_frames (frames before the first IDR and, for CBR, the first seconds are ignored). PSNR / SSIM (luma) of every decoded frame (SSIM every 2th) against the mean image of the stack's own H.264 FixQP reference recording, so the ISP difference between the stacks drops out; sensor noise stays in (see the noise-floor row): an encoder that smooths noise can score higher than the reference. blk = blockiness of the error image (step across 8-px borders / step inside, 1.00 = no block structure); GOP drift = PSNR of the IDR minus the last P of the GOP. n/a = the streamer of that stack did not take the setting.

run-1108-full3k-clogsopenflagReload logs show repeated T20FW switch_wdr/mesh_reload bursts with a ~20 ms stall in one cycle. Phases log reports persistent BAD-uv-static NV12 frames (UV fixed at 128, 7/7 static) on every snapshot, abnormal AE overshoot on lamp-on, and a DAYNIGHT-STUCK failure where the ISP stayed in Night with lamps on, pointing to firmware state and output-path faults. No oops or BUG lines were recorded and the sensor module bind/unbind was clean.
anomalies: reload_dmesg_8.txt: repeated T20FW switch_wdr/mesh_reload cycles (about 8 back-to-back reloads within ~0.006 s) at 13654.858-13655.526, indicating a firmware reload loop or redundant tuning reloads, reload_dmesg_9.txt: same repeated T20FW switch_wdr/mesh_reload burst (about 8 reloads within ~0.03 s, including an unusual gap before table6 done at 13692.801434 to 13692.821016), suggesting firmware timing stalls, reload_dmesg_9.txt: T20FW mesh_reload data done timestamps show a ~20 ms gap (13692.801434 to 13692.821016) inside the reload sequence, a possible firmware timeout symptom, reload_dmesg_8.txt and reload_dmesg_9.txt: 'QBUF guard: rmem window' and codec_set_device MIC messages occur during firmware reload, which may indicate buffer/memory-window handling issues, phases.log: 'snap ok ... layout BAD-uv-static zero_lines even 0 odd 0 uv_static 7/7' on every snapshot, with per-frame UV fixed at 128.00, indicating a frame/UV plane corruption (static chroma) from the driver or firmware output path, phases.log: NV12 frames show uv_static 7/7 and perframeUV 128.00 constant, consistent with a stalled chroma DMA or firmware not updating UV data, phases.log: 'DAYNIGHT-STUCK: ISP still in Night with the lamps on after 180 s (OPEN)' indicates the firmware day/night switching failed to respond to lamp changes, phases.log: 'daycheck: ISP in Night with the lamps on' at 00:15:10 shows ISP mode not updating, consistent with a firmware state machine hang, phases.log: 'RES reload open lamps' and 'settle ... overshoot 85.3 %, peak deviation 136 %' at 23:57:31 show abnormal AE overshoot on lamp-on, a possible firmware AE control issue, phases.log: 'frames 8 ... Ytemporal 2.492' and 'drift 3.63' during night indicate unstable temporal output in firmware processing, phases.log: sensor client is bound before and after insmod each cycle (i2c before=bound after_insmod=bound), so driver bind is consistent; no oops/BUG reported (oops=0); severity: high

run-1108-full3k-clogsvendorflagNo kernel oops, warnings, or RTSP errors were logged, and the RTSP streams and most AE/exposure checks passed. The main driver-related concerns are a persistently bad NV12 chroma layout (U/V stuck at 128, zero-line checks flagged) in night IR snapshots, a failing OSD text overlay check on two attempts, and a forced sysrq reboot to recover after a connection reset at the end of the run.
anomalies: Kernel/driver-relevant: 'snap ok ... layout BAD-uv-static zero_lines even 0 odd 0 uv_static 7/7' appears on every snapshot in the night IR phase (01:11:02 through 01:11:43), and the per-frame UV values are constant at 128.00/128.00, indicating the NV12 chroma plane is static/stuck and the frame layout is bad., Night IR ROW line shows U 0.000 and V 0.000 with Ytemporal 2.414 and drift 0.99, consistent with a frozen chroma path in the ISP/sensor driver output at night., OSD text item check failed twice (01:02:47 attempt and 01:03:07 retry): changed 1.5% and 1.4% of item box against a required >2%, with A/A 0.0%, suggesting the OSD overlay is not being rendered by the stack., Hflip check passed but with a notably low settle time reading ('time to hflip applied = 4 s') and a snapshot-based mirror check, which is fine; no direct error, but noted for completeness., Streamer restarted (streamer up at 01:04:55 and again at 01:05:48) with libimp messages; the second restart is not preceded by an explicit reason in the log, which may indicate an unexplained service restart., Unexpected lines with no context: '30930' and '31491' and '1296' appear as bare numbers between log entries, and a 'REPEAT ck_api_osd' retry occurred, which may indicate interleaved or unlabeled output from the driver., Session ended with 'Read from remote host: Connection reset by peer' and 'client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe' followed by a sysrq reboot to restore the image, a forced recovery that indicates the stack became unresponsive or the link dropped during the d1d4 phase., Device rebooted (uptime 1 min at 01:13:11) and the module list shows tx_isp_t20 and sensor_jxf23_t20 reloaded, which is a reset of the ISP and sensor driver stack.; severity: medium
run-1108-full3k-ccomparebothinfoOpen-source stack looks better overall: more accurate and neutral white balance, more faithful colours (especially reds, pinks and skin-tone patches), and better highlight handling. The vendor stack wins on punchy saturation in yellows and oranges, slightly brighter shadows, and marginally crisper edges. Sharpness and noise are broadly similar in both frames at this resolution.
better_overall: open; open_better: White balance is more neutral: the white and grey patches look closer to true neutral, while the vendor image has a warmer/yellow cast on the greys and whites., Colour accuracy: skin-tone and pastel patches (peach, pink, red) are closer to the chart's reference look, whereas the vendor version pushes oranges and yellows harder and shifts reds toward salmon., Tone and contrast: the open stack keeps the bright white patches less blown out and retains more separation in the light greys., Blues and greens look more natural and less oversaturated in the open image.; vendor_better: Saturation punch: the vendor image is more vivid on the yellow, orange and yellow-green patches, which some viewers may prefer for a lively look., Shadow brightness: the dark grey patch at top-left and overall exposure look slightly lifted in the vendor image., Edge detail on the chart border and patch edges appears marginally crisper in the vendor version, though the difference is small.
run-1108-full3k-ctriagebothinfoOnly the open-stack OSD text item fail looks like a real defect (consistent 1.9 % change, just under the 2 % threshold, with a clean A/A baseline). The open-stack WB settle timeout is unclear and needs a rerun after lamp warm-up. All vendor-stack fails are references and are classed as invalid for our purposes, with the vendor h264 no-decode likely a setup problem.
open time to a stable picture: WB preset 3 at 3000 K: unclear (Settle timeout at 60 s could be a real AWB/preset convergence defect or a light-box flicker/lamp warm-up issue; need to rerun after lamp warm-up and compare against a longer window.) | open OSD text item appears: real (Failed 2/2 with a 1.9 % change against a 2 % threshold while the A/A baseline is 0.0 %, so the text is measurably present but just under the bar; the box and threshold are well defined, pointing to a likely real rendering or size defect rather than noise.) | vendor time to a stable picture: WB preset 1 at 3000 K: invalid (Vendor-stack reference fail only; it is not one of our defects, and the same settle-time setup problem applies to the light box.) | vendor h264 ref_qp10: invalid (No decodable frames after restart suggests a test-setup or stream-handling problem (restart sequencing, decoder not synced) rather than a stack defect; it is a vendor reference anyway.) | vendor OSD text item appears: invalid (Vendor-stack reference fail only; the 1.5 % change at 2/2 failure is a reference result and not a defect of our stack.)
run-1109-5000logsopenflagNo explicit kernel oops, warnings, watchdog timeouts, resets, or repeated driver error messages appear in the logs. The notable items are large AE exposure swings during the lamp on/off tests, unexplained bare numeric lines, a slow initial AE settle, and a non-standard flashed tx_isp/libimp build. Overall the run looks functionally sound, but the exposure swings and flashed-driver status merit follow-up.

Method

  • Same camera, same chart position, same lamps; open stack first, then the vendor ISP module + vendor libimp are loaded from /tmp (nothing flashed); the camera returns to the flashed image at the end (module reload or reboot).
  • P1 = camera defaults (AE, AWB, comp 128). P2 = matched exposure: the same integration time and gains on both stacks, set inside the streamer and read back from the ISP; rows whose read-back differs are marked verify=FAIL and not compared.
  • A/A: point p2_a is measured twice (p2_a, p2_a2); the relative difference is the repeatability of the method. A difference between the stacks counts only beyond 2 x that spread (floor 5 %).
  • NV12 noise is measured on raw NV12 frames from the streamer (no JPEG in the path): temporal standard deviation per pixel over the burst, mean over Y 32..224, and U/V.
  • Colour: SpyderCheckr 24 detected automatically, sRGB -> Lab (D50), CIEDE2000 against the Datacolor default values (D50 assumed, not batch specific); 'grey-normalised' removes the white-balance cast first.
  • Sharpness: slanted-edge method on the chart's outer patch edges, frames averaged against noise; JPEG snapshot path.
  • SSIM/PSNR (when run): both stacks record the same static chart scene at the same bitrate; each stream is decoded and compared against a high-bitrate capture of the SAME stack (reference), so the number is the encoder loss of that stack; a cross-stack comparison on static frames is listed separately and includes the ISP difference.
  • Encoder (A5): both stacks get the same streamer settings (codec, rc_mode, qp / bitrate, gop) through a /tmp conf and a streamer restart; the recordings come over RTSP (ffmpeg -c copy). The reference is a mean image, because single NV12 frames are not frame-aligned with the stream; the scene is static, so every decoded frame can be compared with it. A second reference at the end of the phase shows whether the scene or the AE moved in between.
  • Lamp switches are made by a person on a marker (NEED_* file); the times above are the marker times.
